newsitem.title: GERMANY: Eurobit says WTO infotech pact must be widened.
newsitem.headline: Eurobit says WTO infotech pact must be widened.

text.p: The World Trade Organisation's (WTO) information technology agreement (ITA) is a leap forward, but steps must be taken to ensure it is widely adopted, Eurobit president Bruno Lamborghini said on Friday.
Eurobit, the European Association of Manufacturers of Business Machines and Information Technology Industry, was one of the original proponents of the agreement, coauthoring a version in 1994.

"The ITA is set to ensure a sharp cutback of duties on information and communications technology on a world-wide level," Lamborghini said. "What matters now is that the ITA is geographically expanded and quickly implemented."
Twenty-eight countries agreed on Friday to a pact to eliminate tariffs on a range of high-technology products from computers to telephone headsets by the year 2000.
The deal, at the end of the week-long inaugural ministerial conference of the WTO in Singapore, will cut tariffs in four stages between 1997 and 2000.
Lamborghini said participants must also prevent the shift of information technology products into tariff groups the ITA does not apply to, like consumer electronics, he added.

"If this happens, we have a tariff reduction on paper and a tariff increase through the back door," he said, citing the case of CD-ROM drives previously misclassified by European countries as video recorders with 14 percent import duties.

Lamborghini said EU countries collect more than 1.6 billion ecu of import duties on information and communications technology equipment annually. The adoption of the infotech agreement could cut the price of the average personal computer by 50 ecu, he said.
